translationRepairs: Zhuangzong, the Guangsheng Shenmin Xia emperor, bore the taboo name Cunxu and was Wuhuang's eldest son.
Zhuangzong, the Guangsheng Shenmin Xiao emperor, bore the taboo name Cunxu and was Wuhuang's eldest son.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 孝 is standardly Xiao, not Xia; the posthumous name 光聖神閔孝皇帝 should be romanized Guangsheng Shenmin Xiao.
Wuhuang's uprising at Yunzhong drew elite northern soldiers; when he crushed the rebels and escorted the emperor home, Cunxu's merit stood first.
Wuhuang's uprising at Yunzhong drew elite northern soldiers; when he crushed the rebels and escorted the emperor home, his merit stood first.

Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 功居第一 has no subject change from 武皇起義雲中; the following sentence about spoiling troops also concerns Wuhuang, so the inserted 'Cunxu's merit' is a wrong referent.
He banned brigandage, aided widows and orphans, sought recluses, curbed greed and cruelty, strengthened dikes and prisons—and within a month the realm changed.
He banned brigandage, aided widows and orphans, sought recluses, curbed greed and cruelty, heightened dikes, and eased lawsuits—and within a month the realm changed.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 寬獄訟 means easing prison litigation, not strengthening prisons; 峻堤防 is heightening dikes and defenses only.
In the ninth month Bin, Qi, and Shu struck Chang'an again; Cunxu sent Li Siyuan and Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand against Jinzhou in reply.
In the ninth month Bin, Qi, and Shu struck Chang'an again; Cunxu sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand against Jinzhou in reply.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. Chinese 李嗣昭 is Li Sizhao, a different person from 李嗣源 (Li Siyuan) named earlier in the chapter.
In the ninth month the Bin, Qi, and Shu three commands again mounted a great attack on Chang'an and sent Li Siyuan and Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand troops to attack Jinzhou in response.
In the ninth month the Bin, Qi, and Shu three commands again mounted a great attack on Chang'an and sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand troops to attack Jinzhou in response.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. Chinese 李嗣昭 is Li Sizhao, not Li Siyuan (李嗣源).
In the seventh month of Tianyou 7 Maozhen and Yang Chongben both sent armies to join for a strike on Ling and Xia.
In the seventh month of Tianyou 7 Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Yang Chongben of Binzhou both sent armies to join for a strike on Ling and Xia.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. Idiomatic drops the surnames and postings 鳳翔李茂貞 and 邠州楊崇本 that the Chinese and literal supply.
Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xia, taboo name Cunxu, was the eldest son of Emperor Wuhuang.
Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xiao, taboo name Cunxu, was the eldest son of Emperor Wuhuang.
The paired literal field must use Xiao for 孝, matching the independently reviewed idiomatic correction and structured posthumous-name claim.
